subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After an opted-in deferred-maintenance timeout releases the session lane, should later maintenance requests remain coalesced behind the still-unwinding worker or should OpenClaw introduce a cooperative cancellation/restart contract for context-engine plugins?
rationale: The current context-engine `maintain()` contract does not demonstrate safe concurrent calls or a generic abort mechanism, so choosing between liveness, deferred-maintenance freshness, and plugin concurrency cannot be resolved by a local fence alone.

options.title: Retain worker ownership after timeout
options.body: Recommended: resolve the queued-turn barrier after the bounded persistence checkpoint but retain per-session coalescing until the original maintenance promise settles, avoiding concurrent plugin maintenance.

options.title: Define cooperative cancellation
options.body: Add an explicit, documented context-engine cancellation contract before allowing post-timeout maintenance replacement work to start.

options.title: Accept concurrent reruns
options.body: Land the current behavior only if maintainers explicitly accept that opted-in timeouts may overlap same-session `maintain()` calls for plugins that continue unwinding.

recommendation.title: Retain worker ownership after timeout
recommendation.body: Recommended: resolve the queued-turn barrier after the bounded persistence checkpoint but retain per-session coalescing until the original maintenance promise settles, avoiding concurrent plugin maintenance.
